claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance during high-temperature exposure.
A continuous alumina-based coating a few micrometers thick can be deposited on cast HfNbTaTiZr by physical or chemical vapor deposition.
An adherent alumina layer on HfNbTaTiZr acts as an effective oxygen-diffusion barrier at approximately 1000 °C in air.
The alumina coating prevents oxygen molecules from reaching the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
Blocking oxygen diffusion prevents surface-oxide formation or oxygen segregation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Surface oxides or oxygen segregation would embrittle HfNbTaTiZr.
Preventing oxidation or oxygen segregation preserves the ductility of HfNbTaTiZr during high-temperature service.
Preventing oxidation or oxygen segregation preserves the yield strength of HfNbTaTiZr during high-temperature service.
After 100 hours at approximately 1000 °C in air, coated specimens will have significantly lower oxidation weight gain and less oxide formation than uncoated specimens.
The coated alloy will maintain its baseline ductility and yield strength at 1000 °C relative to the uncoated alloy.
Protection depends on the alumina coating remaining adherent and crack-free during thermal cycling and mechanical strain.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between alumina and HfNbTaTiZr can compromise coating effectiveness.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mediator state that the coating will prevent oxidation and oxygen access, whereas the predicted outcome only requires significantly reduced oxidation, which is a weaker claim permitting residual oxidation.

The stated baseline ductility is a room-temperature value, but the predicted outcome refers to maintaining baseline ductility at 1000 °C. The main post-exposure test is again at room temperature, so it does not directly establish the claimed preservation of ductility under 1000 °C loading.
